text.p: U.S.-based Anadarko Petroleum Corp. will begin a seismic survey of its concession in the Red Sea off Eritrea in November and hopes to begin drilling within a year, a company official said Monday.

"A seismic ship will arrive to Massawa late October. The seismic survey will start in the beginning of November and go on until January," company vice-president and general manager Barclay Collins told Reuters.
"We plan to start drilling this time next year, during the third quarter," he said, adding that the first studies had shown some promise.
"It is too early to say, even though the background studies have been encouraging. They showed indication of hydrocarbons."

Houston-based Anadarko signed an agreement with the Eritrean government last year under which it plans to spend $30 million during an eight-year concession on the 27,400 sq km (10,275 square mile) Zula block.
